facts.claim: The Macedon Ranges is a region in Central Victoria between Melbourne and Bendigo, known for native forests, an arts scene, food and wine and natural attractions such as Hanging Rock and Mount Macedon.
Hanging Rock is a mamelon formed 6.25 million years ago by stiff lava oozing from a vent; it rises to 718 m and was the setting of Joan Lindsay's novel Picnic at Hanging Rock (1967), filmed in 1975.
Mount Macedon's Camel's Hump, 1,001 m, is the highest peak in the region and is at times covered in snow; snow falls on 15-20 days a year.
The region has more working artists per capita than anywhere else in Victoria, and winters are colder and summers hotter than Melbourne's.

The regional tourism site lists Kyneton, Woodend, Mount Macedon, Macedon, Malmsbury, Lancefield, Gisborne, Riddells Creek and Romsey as villages, with markets, open gardens, botanic gardens and peony picking.

experiences: Hike and picnic among granite and volcanic rock at Hanging Rock
Wander historic villages, cafes and markets
Visit cool-climate gardens and lookouts on Mount Macedon

tips.title: Colder than Melbourne
tips.detail: Mount Macedon sits above 1,000 m and sees snow most winters. Pack a layer even when the city is mild.

tips.title: Drive between villages
tips.detail: Towns and sights are spread across about 1,750 sq km, so a car is the practical way to link villages, gardens and Hanging Rock.

tips.title: Check garden opening dates
tips.detail: Open gardens and peony picking run on set seasons and dates. Check the regional site before you go.

best_months.rationale: Editorial from climate facts (hotter summers, colder snowy winters than Melbourne), so milder autumn and spring suit hiking and gardens; no source states best months.

facts.claim: Lorne is a Great Ocean Road town about two hours from Melbourne (138 km), which began as a logging town.

The section of the Great Ocean Road from Lorne to Apollo Bay was finished in November 1932; the road was built by returned soldiers between 1919 and 1932 and is called the world's largest war memorial.
Teddy's Lookout at the end of George Street offers views over the town, coastline and Great Ocean Road.
Erskine Falls, a 35.49 m single-drop waterfall on the Erskine River, lies immediately outside Lorne in the Otway Ranges.
Lorne has a main beach of about 3 km for bathing and surfing, a pier for fishing, the Great Ocean Road Museum, galleries and cafes along Mountjoy Parade, and borders Great Otway National Park.

experiences: Swim and surf at Lorne's long main beach
Chase waterfalls through Otway fern gullies
Drive the Great Ocean Road coast
Browse cafes and galleries on Mountjoy Parade

tips.title: New Year weekend crowds
tips.detail: Over 20,000 people visit on the first weekend of January for the Pier to Pub swim and surf events. Book ahead and expect crowds.

tips.title: Take care on steep roads
tips.detail: The road up to Teddy's Lookout is steep. Drive carefully.

tips.title: Summer fills the town
tips.detail: Holiday-makers fill Lorne to bursting every summer, so arrive early or visit outside school holidays.

best_months.rationale: Mild summers per climate section (oceanic climate, mild summers, cool damp winters) suit beach time; summer is also the busiest period, so Mar is quieter. Editorial inference.

facts.claim: Beechworth was a gold-producing region and centre of government between 1852 and 1857, and its logo is a golden horseshoe from an 1855 election candidate who rode a horse shod in gold.
The historic precinct has well-preserved gold-rush buildings including the Court House, Burke Museum and Ned Kelly connections; Ned Kelly spent time in HM Prison Beechworth.
Attractions include the Ned Kelly-themed courthouse displays, Burke Museum, waterfalls, gunpowder magazine, Spring Creek Gorge, ghost tours, Beechworth Bakery, brewery and wineries.
The town is at 560 m and has a cool climate much of the year, more like central Victoria; it is one end of the Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail.
Beechworth is about 284 km from Melbourne and can be reached from the Hume Freeway at Wangaratta or Wodonga.

experiences: Walk gold-rush streets and heritage buildings
Cycle the Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail
Taste honey, bakery treats and local wine

tips.title: Bring your own car
tips.detail: There is no car hire in Beechworth, so arrive with a vehicle or plan to walk the compact historic centre.

tips.title: Hire bikes for the rail trail
tips.detail: The old railway line to Wangaratta and Bright is a paved rail trail, and bicycles can be hired in town.

tips.title: Easter festival crowds
tips.detail: The Golden Horseshoes Festival parade at Easter and the August Ned Kelly Weekend bring crowds. Book stays early.

best_months.rationale: Editorial from cool 560 m climate; autumn and spring are mild for walking and cycling. No source states best months.

facts.claim: The park was created in December 1995, covers 76,003 ha of wet mountain ash forest and cool temperate rainforest in the Great Dividing Range, and is home to Mountain Ash, the world's tallest flowering tree.
Mount Donna Buang (1,245 m) has a 21 m lookout tower with views over Melbourne, the Yarra Valley and the Dandenong and Cathedral Ranges, and is Melbourne's closest winter snow playground.
The Rainforest Gallery is a 40 m viewing platform perched 15 m above the forest floor near Warburton.
The Black Spur Drive winds through Mountain Ash forest from Healesville to Narbethong, and Lady Talbot Drive passes rainforest walks and waterfalls near Marysville.
84% of the park lies in a closed water supply catchment that supplies about 70% of Melbourne's water, so most of it is closed to the public.

experiences: Walk among the world's tallest flowering trees
Drive the Black Spur and Lady Talbot Drive
See Melbourne's nearest snow on Mount Donna Buang

tips.title: Most of the park is closed
tips.detail: Most of the park protects Melbourne's drinking water and is closed to visitors. Stay on signed tracks and roads.

tips.title: No facilities in the park
tips.detail: There are no shops or services inside the park. Stock up in Healesville, Marysville or Warburton.

best_months.rationale: Editorial: warm-season walking and driving; winter (Jun-Aug) suits snowplay at Donna Buang per Parks Victoria. No source states best months.

seasonal_tags.note: Mount Donna Buang is described as Melbourne's closest winter playground; snow cover varies by year.
